newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller faces further corruption vote.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller faces further corruption vote.

text.p: Turkey's parliament is to vote on Wednesday whether to send Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court on corruption charges dating from her three years as premier.
Parliament officials said MPs would gather at 1500 (1300 GMT) for a debate and vote on opposition allegations that Ciller's large personal wealth is a result of illegal enrichment.
Ciller won two corruption votes on Tuesday and MPs said she was also likely to weather the latest ballot.
The Islamist-led coalition would be badly shaken if Ciller were impeached but her opponents on paper are around six MPs short of the 276 votes they need to guarantee victory.

The opposition's best showing in Tuesday's votes was 257 votes against Ciller, who was prime minister between 1993 and 1996. She now also serves as foreign minister and head of the conservative True Path Party junior coalition partner.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's government must deal with an opposition censure motion next week that accuses it of threatening Turkey's secular system with plans to increase the role of Islam in public life.
